input.question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?
input.ground_truth: The kidneys and eyes have a higher concentration of capillaries than other organs. High sugar levels in the blood cause capillary damage, thus the two are affected more. Here is an article from [_URL_3_](_URL_0_) and one from another [Reddit post](_URL_1_) in [r/diabetes](_URL_2_). Retino = eyes, Nephro = kidney, -pathy = denoting disorder in a part of the body. & #x200B; Hope that helps. & #x200B; R

Okay! Let’s imagine your body is like a house, and all the little rooms in the house are different organs, like the kitchen (which is like your stomach), the bedroom (like your heart), and the bathroom (like your kidneys), and your eyes are like the windows.

Now, when someone has type 2 diabetes, it’s like there’s too much sugar in the blood, kind of like if you spilled a bunch of sugar all over your house. Usually, the sugar should be cleaned up by a helper called insulin, but in type 2 diabetes, the helper doesn’t work as well.

Now, the kidneys (the bathroom) and the eyes (the windows) are very sensitive to sugar. If there’s too much sugar in the blood for a long time, it can start to hurt the kidneys and the tiny blood vessels in the eyes.

- **Kidneys** get too much sugar and over time, the sugar can damage the filters in the kidneys. It’s like if you left a glass of sweet juice in the bathroom for a long time—the bathroom gets damaged and can’t clean the house as well.

- **Eyes** have very tiny blood vessels, like super thin straws. When there’s too much sugar, those straws can get hurt and start to leak. That’s why we call it “diabetic retinopathy”—it’s like the windows get cloudy or broken because of the sugar.

Other parts of the body can also get hurt by too much sugar, but the kidneys and eyes are like the most sensitive to it. That’s why doctors watch them very closely when someone has type 2 diabetes.
